name: sim_determinism_across_a_stall
description: A stalled client ends where the others do (design 6.7 and 6.8, M4): three clients play High Water, and in wave 3 client 3's loop stops for 20 s, as a hidden tab or a long hitch does, while the others play on. After 5 s of its silence the server's AWAY hands seat 3 to the caretaker; halfway through the stall a fourth client joins from client 1's checkpoint, as a rejoin does. Then client 3 catches up 8 ticks a frame, running the AWAY, the caretaker's choices for its own seat and its partners' orders in one burst, and BACK returns its seat at the next window. Every hash of all four clients agrees, every field of every record matches, the seat moved at the same ticks on every client, and a fresh replay of the turn log reproduces every hash.

steps.msg: the others have seat 3 away while client 3 stands 600 ticks back, still thinking it present
client 3 sat out 20 s; the client joined from the checkpoint kept up
it caught up in 150 frames of 8 ticks, and now knows its seat away

steps.assert: moves.size() == 3 and moves[0][1] == 'away' and moves[1][1] == 'returning' and moves[2][1] == 'present'
steps.msg: away, returning, and back at the window

steps.assert: scene.seat_moves(3, 2) == moves and scene.seat_moves(3, 3) == moves and scene.seat_moves(3, 4) == [moves[1], moves[2]]
steps.msg: at the same ticks on every client, the stalled one too
the caretaker's choices for its seat ran on client 3 in the burst
every hash agrees across the four clients
and every field of every record
a fresh replay of the turn log reproduces every hash
